newsitem.title: UK: LME end-users want greater say in exchange board.
newsitem.headline: LME end-users want greater say in exchange board.

text.p: Metal producers and consumers want greater representation on the board of the London Metal Exchange (LME), replies to a major market review show.
The review is being undertaken by Britain's senior financial regulator the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) in the wake of the Sumitomo Corp $2.6 billion copper losses.
But David Pritchard, head of the SIB's markets and exchanges division, who is heading the review, told Reuters there is no agreement as to what form such a restructuring of the LME board should take.
"But there does seem to be a call from producers and consumers for a rebalancing of the board so that they have a greater say in the operation of the LME," Pritchard said.
So far the SIB has received 50 responses to a 33-question document it has distributed to all sections of the metals industry although some of these have come from large trade bodies.

Most of the responses call for a change in the make-up of the exchange's governing body so that there are fewer LME traders. One objective is to avoid potential conflicts of interest on things like supervision and surveillance.
At the moment the 16-strong LME board is dominated by its ring-dealing membership but does include representatives of producers and consumers.

Outside its public consultation on the metal markets SIB is looking at how the LME is governed. The comments in the responses came in answer to a general catch-all question asking for any other strongly held views.
